name: VARP
description: VARP calculates the variance based on an entire population, using the n denominator. It is the legacy compatibility version of VAR.P.
tldr: Population variance (n) of a set of numbers.

parameters.name: number1
parameters.description: The first number, range, or reference in the population.

parameters.name: number2
parameters.description: Additional numbers, ranges, or references (optional, up to 255 total arguments).

basicExample.explanation: The mean is 30; the sum of squared deviations is 1000, divided by 5 gives a population variance of 200.

advancedExamples.title: Population from a range
advancedExamples.scenario: Full census of a small group
advancedExamples.description: Compute the variance of every value in B2:B6
advancedExamples.explanation: Divides by n (5) rather than n-1.

advancedExamples.title: Population vs sample
advancedExamples.explanation: VARP divides by 5 (n) while VAR divides by 4 (n-1), so the sample version is larger. VARP is the square of STDEVP.

howItWorks: VARP computes the population variance as the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by n. Using n (not n-1) is correct only when the supplied data is the complete population; for a sample, VAR's n-1 correction is appropriate. Text and logical values in references are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Confirm population
howToSteps.text: Ensure the data represents the entire population, not a sample.

limitations: Only valid when the data is the entire population; using it on a sample underestimates the true variance.
Ignores text and logical values inside ranged references.
Requires at least one numeric value, otherwise returns #DIV/0!.

commonErrors.fix: Provide at least one data point.

commonErrors.cause: Data was actually a sample but n was used.
commonErrors.fix: Use VAR (or VAR.S) for a sample.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: VARP behaves the same in Google Sheets as a population variance.

faq.question: What is the difference between VARP and VAR?
faq.answer: VARP divides by n (population), VAR divides by n-1 (sample).

faq.question: Is VARP the same as VAR.P?
faq.answer: Functionally yes; VAR.P is the modern replacement for the legacy VARP.

faq.question: How is VARP related to STDEVP?
faq.answer: VARP is the square of STDEVP for the same data set.
